name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
common_uses: Temporary relief of mild to moderate pain (headaches, muscle aches, toothaches, backaches)
Reduction of fever associated with common colds, viral infections, or flu
common_side_effects: Generally well-tolerated at recommended therapeutic doses
Rare: Nausea, mild stomach discomfort, skin rash or allergic reactions
important_precautions: Do NOT exceed 4,000 mg (4 grams) in 24 hours for healthy adults (often recommended lower at 3,000 mg to prevent liver strain)
Check labels of all multi-symptom cold/flu medications to avoid accidental double dosing
Individuals with liver impairment, chronic hepatitis, or alcohol dependency must consult a physician before use
Keep strictly out of reach of children and use calibrated dosing syringes for pediatric liquid suspensions
known_interactions: Alcohol: Significantly increases risk of severe liver toxicity
Warfarin: Chronic high-dose paracetamol may modestly enhance anticoagulant effect
Other acetaminophen-containing products (NyQuil, Tylenol PM, Excedrin, etc.)
overdose_warning: ACUTE LIVER FAILURE: Paracetamol overdose is a medical emergency requiring immediate administration of N-acetylcysteine. Seek emergency care immediately if an overdose is suspected.
educational_disclaimer: This monograph is for educational informational purposes only. Do not self-prescribe, alter doses, or discontinue medications without consulting a licensed physician or pharmacist.

name: Ibuprofen (Advil / Motrin)
common_uses: Relief of pain and inflammation from arthritis, sprains, strains, menstrual cramps, dental pain
common_side_effects: Stomach upset, heartburn, nausea, abdominal pain
important_precautions: Always take with food or milk to minimize gastrointestinal irritation
Avoid if you have a history of stomach ulcers, gastrointestinal bleeding, or severe kidney disease
NSAIDs increase the risk of heart attack or stroke, especially with prolonged use or pre-existing cardiac conditions
Avoid during the third trimester of pregnancy due to risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus
known_interactions: Blood thinners (Aspirin, Warfarin, Apixaban): Heightened risk of major GI bleeding
ACE Inhibitors / ARBs / Diuretics: May reduce antihypertensive efficacy and harm renal function
Corticosteroids: Multiplies risk of peptic ulceration
Alcohol: Increases gastrointestinal bleeding risks
overdose_warning: Symptoms of overdose include lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, and metabolic acidosis. Seek urgent emergency care.
educational_disclaimer: This monograph is for educational informational purposes only. Do not self-prescribe, alter doses, or discontinue medications without consulting a licensed physician or pharmacist.

name: Amoxicillin
common_uses: Treatment of susceptible bacterial infections: middle ear infections (otitis media), strep throat, bacterial pneumonia, skin infections, urinary tract infections
Part of combination therapy for Helicobacter pylori eradication
common_side_effects: Mild non-allergic skin rash, oral or vaginal candidiasis (thrush/yeast infection)
important_precautions: Antibiotics are COMPLETELY INEFFECTIVE against viral illnesses like the common cold, COVID-19, or influenza
Complete the entire prescribed course even if symptoms resolve earlier to prevent bacterial resistance
STRICT CONTRAINDICATION in patients with true penicillin anaphylaxis or severe hypersensitivity
Seek emergency care immediately if wheezing, facial swelling, or severe blistering rash occurs
known_interactions: Methotrexate: Penicillins may decrease clearance and increase methotrexate toxicity
Probenecid: Increases and prolongs amoxicillin serum concentrations
Oral contraceptives: May potentially reduce efficacy; secondary contraception is advised by some guidelines
overdose_warning: Overdose is generally associated with severe gastrointestinal symptoms and crystalluria. Maintain adequate hydration and seek immediate medical evaluation.
educational_disclaimer: This is a prescription-only antimicrobial. Never use leftover antibiotics without clinical diagnosis and prescription by a licensed practitioner.

name: Metformin
common_uses: First-line pharmacological treatment for type 2 diabetes mellitus to improve glycemic control
Off-label management of polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) and prediabetes
common_side_effects: Gastrointestinal disturbances: diarrhea, nausea, abdominal discomfort, metallic taste, bloating
Long-term use may lead to reduced Vitamin B12 absorption
important_precautions: Take with meals to diminish gastrointestinal adverse effects; extended-release formulations may improve tolerability
BOXED WARNING: Lactic acidosis is a rare but life-threatening complication, particularly in severe renal impairment, sepsis, or acute heart failure
Temporarily discontinue prior to iodinated radiocontrast procedures as directed by your physician
Routine monitoring of renal function (eGFR) and serum B12 levels is essential
known_interactions: Excessive alcohol intake: Strongly enhances risk of lactic acidosis and hypoglycemia
Iodinated contrast media: Risk of acute renal impairment and subsequent metformin accumulation
Cimetidine and cationic drugs: May increase systemic metformin exposure
overdose_warning: Metformin overdose carries a high risk of severe lactic acidosis with hypothermia, hypotension, and somnolence. Requires emergency hemodialysis.
educational_disclaimer: Prescription medication. Do not adjust diabetes medication regimens without endocrinology or primary care oversight.

name: Cetirizine (Zyrtec)
common_uses: Relief of symptoms associated with seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, itchy watery eyes)
Treatment of uncomplicated skin manifestations of chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives)
common_side_effects: Mild drowsiness / somnolence (less common than first-generation antihistamines, but higher than fexofenadine)
important_precautions: Caution while operating motor vehicles or machinery until you know how it affects your alertness
Dose adjustments may be necessary for patients with moderate to severe renal or hepatic impairment
Avoid concurrent central nervous system depressants
known_interactions: Alcohol and sedatives: Additive sedation and psychomotor impairment
Theophylline: May produce a small decrease in cetirizine clearance
overdose_warning: Overdose may produce severe somnolence in adults, or agitation and restlessness followed by drowsiness in children. Contact poison control immediately.
educational_disclaimer: This monograph is for educational informational purposes only. Consult a healthcare provider if allergy symptoms persist or worsen.

name: Omeprazole (Prilosec)
common_uses: Treatment of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis
Healing and prevention of duodenal and gastric ulcers
common_side_effects: Headache, abdominal pain, diarrhea, constipation, nausea, flatulence
important_precautions: Take 30 to 60 minutes before the first meal of the day on an empty stomach for maximum acid suppression
Do not crush or chew delayed-release capsules or tablets
Long-term use (>1 year) is associated with increased risk of bone fractures, hypomagnesemia, vitamin B12 deficiency, and Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea
Prompt medical evaluation is needed if warning signs such as involuntary weight loss, dysphagia, or vomiting blood occur
known_interactions: Clopidogrel (Plavix): Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, decreasing clopidogrel's antiplatelet activation
Ketoconazole, Itraconazole, Iron supplements: Decreased absorption due to increased gastric pH
Methotrexate: Concomitant PPI use may elevate methotrexate levels
overdose_warning: Symptoms of overdose include confusion, drowsiness, blurred vision, tachycardia, and diaphoresis. Supportive medical care is indicated.
educational_disclaimer: Educational reference only. Persistent acid reflux should be evaluated by a healthcare professional to rule out Barrett's esophagus or other conditions.

name: Atorvastatin (Lipitor)
common_uses: Lowering elevated low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), total cholesterol, and triglycerides
Primary and secondary cardiovascular risk reduction for myocardial infarction and stroke in high-risk patients
common_side_effects: Myalgia (muscle ache or stiffness), arthralgia, diarrhea, dyspepsia
Mild asymptomatic elevation in liver transaminases, small increase in HbA1c/blood glucose
important_precautions: Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness immediately, particularly if accompanied by malaise or dark/tea-colored urine (rhabdomyolysis warning)
Strictly contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent elevations in hepatic transaminases
Contraindicated during pregnancy and breastfeeding
known_interactions: Grapefruit juice in large amounts (>1 liter/day): Inhibits CYP3A4, substantially elevating atorvastatin concentrations
Clarithromycin, Itraconazole, Protease inhibitors: Substantially increase myopathy risk
Gemfibrozil: Increased risk of severe myopathy/rhabdomyolysis
overdose_warning: No specific antidote exists. In case of acute overdose, support vital functions and monitor hepatic and CPK enzymes.
educational_disclaimer: Educational guide only. Never stop statin therapy abruptly without consulting your cardiologist or prescribing physician.

name: Aspirin (Acetylsalicylic Acid)
common_uses: Secondary cardiovascular prevention (low-dose 81mg 'baby aspirin') for ischemic stroke and myocardial infarction
Immediate emergency administration during suspected acute myocardial infarction (chewed, unless contraindicated)
Temporary relief of mild pain and fever (at higher analgesic doses)
common_side_effects: Gastric irritation, heartburn, easy bruising, prolonged bleeding time
important_precautions: NEVER give aspirin to children or teenagers recovering from viral infections (chickenpox/flu) due to the risk of REYE'S SYNDROME (fatal encephalopathy and liver damage)
High risk of gastrointestinal ulceration and hemorrhage
Contraindicated in active bleeding disorders, severe asthma with nasal polyps (aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease)
known_interactions: Other anticoagulants and antiplatelets (Warfarin, Heparin, Clopidogrel): Multiplied hemorrhage risk
Other NSAIDs (Ibuprofen): May interfere with the cardioprotective antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin if taken simultaneously
Alcohol: Dramatically elevates gastric mucosal bleeding
overdose_warning: Salicylate toxicity causes tinnitus (ringing in ears), hyperventilation, vomiting, hyperthermia, and profound metabolic acidosis. Seek urgent medical emergency treatment.
educational_disclaimer: Do not start daily preventive aspirin therapy without an individualized cardiovascular and bleeding risk discussion with your doctor.
